title: Loukidis et al. (2003) slope at its critical seismic coefficient, dry

meta.title: Loukidis et al. (2003) slope at its critical seismic coefficient, dry
meta.notes: 25 m high 3:1 slope, c′ = 25 kPa, φ′ = 30°, γ = 20 kN/m³, dry, with the horizontal seismic coefficient kh = 0.432, Loukidis, Bandini & Salgado's critical value; critical-surface searches.

source.reference: Loukidis, D., Bandini, P. & Salgado, R. (2003). Stability of seismically loaded slopes using limit analysis. Géotechnique 53(5), 463–479.
source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V102a (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: The critical seismic coefficients (dry 0.432, rᵤ = 0.5 0.132) are Loukidis, Bandini & Salgado's, quoted identically by commercial program A (verification problem 62) and commercial program B (§2.38); the paper itself (paywalled) was not consulted. They are defined as the horizontal coefficient at which F = 1, from a log-spiral mechanism; both manuals give 'Loukidis factor of safety (Spencer) = 1.000'.

Geometry and soil from both manuals' figures and tables and a third program's example script of the same problem: 25 m high 3:1 slope from the toe (0, 0) to the crest (75, 25), ground from x = −50 to 150, base at −25; c′ = 25 kPa, φ′ = 30°, γ = 20 kN/m³. Both manuals restrict the circles to the toe; cSlope's unrestricted search ends at the toe as well.
Commercial program A's non-circular values (path search with optimization): Spencer 0.999, Bishop 0.989.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
